title: They look alive in church.
paragraphs:
You can sing every song…
and still be spiritually numb.

You can say “Amen”…
and never say “Yes” to Jesus.
And here’s the tension you can’t escape:
What if your faith feels real… but isn’t?

What if the danger isn’t rebellion—
but comfort?
while still sitting in the pew.
There is a kind of Christianity that feels safe.

Clean on the outside.
Disciplined in routine.
Polite. Presentable. Predictable.

No fire.
No trembling.
No real hunger for God.

You pray, but it’s mechanical.
You read the Bible, but nothing burns.
You worship, but your heart stays distant.
You just don’t want Him deeply anymore.
Not cold enough to run away.
And Jesus says that middle place is dangerous.

Not because He hates you—
but because He loves you too much to leave you there.
Let’s go straight to the Word.
“I know your works: you are neither cold nor hot. Would that you were either cold or hot! So, because you are lukewarm, and neither hot nor cold, I will spit you out of my mouth.”

Not a preacher.
Not a prophet.
Jesus.
And He’s not talking to atheists.

People who gathered.
People who believed.
People who thought they were fine.
“For you say, I am rich, I have prospered, and I need nothing, not realizing that you are wretched, pitiable, poor, blind, and naked.”
This is the great deception of lukewarm faith:

You can feel spiritually secure…
while actually being spiritually empty.

You can measure your life by blessings—
and completely miss your brokenness.

You can say, “I’m okay”—
while your soul is starving.

This is not about how loud you sing.
Not about how often you attend church.
Not about how many Bible verses you can quote.
This is about your heart before Jesus.
Or just the life He improves?
Or just fit Him into your schedule?
Lukewarm faith often hides behind religious performance.

You serve… but you’re empty.
You give… but there’s no joy.
You show up… but your heart checked out long ago.
Jesus becomes a background character in your life.

Not Lord.
Not King.
Just… an accessory.
Some scholars interpret the “lukewarm” imagery in Revelation as referencing Laodicea’s water system—water that arrived neither hot nor cold, but tepid and unpleasant.

Not refreshing like cold water.
Not healing like hot springs.

Not evil in appearance.
Just ineffective in reality.
Lukewarmness is not just about behavior.
Your heart has found satisfaction somewhere else.

The same Jesus who warns—
also invites.

“Those whom I love, I reprove and discipline, so be zealous and repent. Behold, I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in to him and eat with him, and he with me.”
You and I are not just “a little off.”

Not just by action—
but by nature.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.”
And sin does not lead to inconvenience.
“For the wages of sin is death…”
Because lukewarmness is still a heart that resists full surrender to God.
But God did not leave us there.
But when we were broken, distracted, divided.
“But God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”
Jesus Christ stepped into our place.
He lived the life we could not live.
Then He went to the cross—

Your hidden sin was seen.
Your apathy was exposed.
Your divided heart was accounted for.
He absorbed the wrath of God that we deserved.

Proving sin is defeated.
Death is broken.
Grace is alive.
But here is where everything turns:
“Repent therefore, and turn back, that your sins may be blotted out.”

From self → to Christ.
From control → to surrender.
From lukewarm → to alive.
Jesus is not asking for a better version of you.
He is calling for your whole heart.
Some of you reading this feel exposed.
Not because this is condemning you—
You remember when your heart burned.

When worship felt real.
When prayer felt alive.
When Jesus wasn’t just a concept—
but your everything.
You are not too far gone.
But you are being called back.

Not with anger—
but with nail-scarred hands.

Not to shame you—
but to restore you.

Not to push you away—
but to bring you close.
“Jesus, I don’t want lukewarm faith anymore.”

With grace.
With mercy.
With presence.
Come back to it when your heart starts drifting again.
And if this stirred something deep in you…
